newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Market takes breather after ride.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Market takes breather after ride.

text.p: U.S. stock index options dealers and investors took a breather Thursday after Wednesday's wild ride which some market participants said encompassed the kind of action not seen since 1987.
"I would suspect it's going to be kind of a working vacation for the next day or two," one options dealer said. "Volume's down a little bit here today. The action yesterday exhausted some people."
On Wednesday, September S&P 500 futures traded in a 25-point range, while the blue chip Dow 30 average .DJI traded in a 161-point range.
Most of the ranges were carved out within the first hour of trading as participants digested some July sales and wholesale inflation data.
"I can only describe yesterday's market action as the most volatile since the aftermath of the '87 crash," Jon Najarian, president of Mercury Trading in Chicago, said in a reprt.
"Most traders were exhausted within the first hour and a half," he said.
Gregory Nie, a technical analyst at Everen Securities, said sessions of extremely wide swings in the Dow and other market measures were likely to become more frequent.
"It's a continuation of the trend of growing volatility that we've been going through for three years, with it becoming much more visible this year," he said.
"Two-hundred-point up-days (on the Dow), 300-point down-days are really minor moves given the price level that we've achieved," he added.
But on Thursday, a much calmer reaction was seen to the July U.S. consumer price report, which met expectations.
By about 1155 CDT/1640 GMT, the Dow was up six points at 7,934, having traded between about 7,929 and 7,998.
September S&P 500 futures were up 3.60 at 929.40, off their 934 session high.
The spot S&P 500 index .SPX gained 3.19 to 925.21 and the S&P 100 .OEX was up 2.21 at 898.24.
Some of the slowdown in index options trading was partly because much of the activity related to the expiration of August options was out of the way, traders said.
"By this afternoon, most of the expiration stuff will be done," the options trader said. "There will be very little left to do."
He said Wedensday's volatility gave a lot of index option investors the opportunity to get any expiration-related trading out of the way.

Moby Waller, an analyst at Investment Research Institute in Cincinnati, said open interest in the OEX August series was relatively low to begin with, which could indicate Friday's expiration will have little impact on the market.

Some traders have noted that although stocks have moved higher during most expiration weeks this year, they have declined on expiration Fridays. The Dow fell 130 points on the expiration Friday in July.
